paper.title: Algorithm 777: HOMPACK90: a suite of Fortran 90 codes for globally convergent homotopy algorithms
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 23(4), 514 (Dec 1997); netlib TOMS 777
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (paywalled). The author list is taken from the funnel item (four authors as listed there); the archive README should be checked for the full list. The claim rests on the shipped expected output RES3 of the archive's driver3.

code.note: Fortran 90 shar archive. Drop everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run with /bin/sh in a fresh directory outside the site (it creates Doc, Drivers, Info and Src). It contains template.f, driver1.f, driver2.f, driver3.f, hompack90.f, lapack.f, blas1-3.f, RES1, RES2, RES3. Build hompack90.f with lapack.f, blas*.f and driver3.f using gfortran, run it, and compare the FIXPQS storage-mode-1 block with the shipped RES3.

claim.location: The shipped expected output RES3 (archive member, produced by driver3.f): the block 'TESTING FIXPQS WITH STORAGE MODE = 1', first solution component on the first printed row, 4.00864019E-01. The driver prints the solution at lambda = 1 (Y(1:8)) with ES16.8. The paper was not read; no paper table or page is cited.

reference.file: 777.gz member RES3 (driver3 expected output), block FIXPQS storage mode 1, Y(1)

claim.metric: Y(1) at lambda = 1 returned by FIXPQS (the fixed-point solution of the driver's homotopy, storage mode 1), as printed in RES3.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read; the value is the one in the shipped RES3.

values.name: FIXPQS storage mode 1, solution component Y(1) at lambda=1

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. RES3 prints the value to 9 significant figures (ES16.8), so rounding alone allows 5e-9 absolute; 1e-8 allows that and nothing more. The endpoint at lambda = 1 is set by the corrector tolerance ANSRE = 1e-12 in driver3, not by the arc-length step, so a different path length from compiler rounding should not move it past 1e-8. Not to be loosened after any run.

claim.note: Chosen over the ARC LENGTH and Jacobian-evaluation counts. Timing lines are machine-dependent and are not used. Only the first component is checked; the other seven are printed to the same precision and are not part of this single claim.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: gfortran compile of hompack90.f with lapack and blas files, and one run of driver3 (FIXPQS, FIXPNS and FIXPDS in two storage modes).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic Fortran 90 homotopy solver whose shipped driver prints a fixed-point solution that depends on the corrector and predictor actually running, not on a value derivable on paper.
